Subject: Clarify: DPA notification timing variance & subprocessor evidence routing

Hi Karthik / Kimberly,

Thanks for the slides last week — Cerulean's legal and security teams reviewed and we have a couple of follow-ups before we can sign the DPA appendix. Primary concerns:

- Your standard incident notification window is 72 hours; we need clarity on how that interacts with (a) time needed to request evidence from subprocessors and (b) international transfer restrictions if the forensic artifacts sit in a non-US jurisdiction.
- Can Redwood commit to a bilateral escalation path if a subprocessor delays evidence handover due to local law? What are the contractual remedies / interim commitments (e.g., snapshot escrow, redacted telemetry export) you can provide within the notification window?
- We need a clear operational owner at Redwood we can call for urgent evidence requests; list of people and escalation tiers.

Could you propose a short mutual action plan (MAP) and note any SLA variance we should expect for subprocessor-involved evidence? We want to avoid ambiguous "cooperation" language that leaves us waiting.

Appreciate a compact plan by EOD tomorrow so our procurement team knows whether to proceed to redlines.

Best,
Jamie Ortega
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Data Security
Cerulean Health

Jamie — thanks for the clear asks. I put together a short MAP and a proposed routing for subprocessor delays; attaching two artifacts: "redwood-proposed-MAP-20260921.pdf" and an export of the current subprocessor roster. High-level answers below and the MAP has the operational commitments.

Summary answers:
- Notification window: Redwood's default is 72 hours for initial notification. Forensics/evidence handover that requires subprocessor cooperation may have a secondary window of up to 14 days depending on jurisdictional constraints. We commit to providing an initial forensic snapshot (redacted as needed) within 72 hours when feasible and a targeted plan for final evidence transfer within 14 days.
- Interim remedies: when a subprocessor cites local law, Redwood will (a) provide a time-stamped forensic snapshot stored under escrow with a neutral third party where permitted, (b) offer redacted telemetry sufficient for triage within 72 hours, and (c) engage a joint forensics call within 48 hours. These are operational commitments — the MAP clarifies when they become binding (subject to DPA clauses + regulatory restrictions).
- Escalation contacts: Primary: Kimberly Park (Privacy Ops) — kimberly_park@redwood.com; Secondary: Marissa Cole (Security Liaison) — marissa_cole@redwood.com; Legal escalation: Karthik Iyer (Data Privacy) — karthik_iyer@redwood.com. We propose a 24/7 pager window for incidents meeting the "material data exposure" threshold; details are in the MAP.

Notes on cross-border export: if evidence export is blocked by local law, Redwood will propose a narrow data slice for remote review under an NDA and provide attestations about what remains on the subprocessor side. Where permissible we'll coordinate a certified third-party review and share findings.

I understand Cerulean needs clarity for procurement — MAP includes acceptance criteria and a fallback SLA variance clause that limits exposure and preserves your remediation rights. If you want, we can redline the specific DPA paragraph tonight.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
